page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address. The x86_64 CPU architecture supports AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets, while lacking AVX-512 extensions.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests all scoring in the middle 50%. Single-core performance presents a mixed profile: Geekbench single-core and text processing benchmarks rank in the top 25%, whereas stress-ng single-core performance falls in the bottom 10%. Memory performance shows average read bandwidth for both small and large blocks, but large-block write bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput is also weak, falling in the bottom 25%. For LLM workloads, prompt processing with a 7B model is average, but text generation with the same model is poor, landing in the bottom 10%.

The shared CPU allocation model offers a cost-efficient hardware profile for workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU execution. However, this shared resource model introduces potential performance variability under sustained high loads. The lack of bundled local storage requires external storage attachments, which is a key architectural tradeoff. Given these parameters, this server is configured for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, text processing, and database operations that can tolerate shared CPU resources and do not demand high-speed local disk I/O.
